title: Perplexity Launches Orchestrator API for Model Routing and Failover
summary: Perplexity's Orchestrator API gives one endpoint for 45+ models with automatic failover and no platform fee. How it stacks up against OpenRouter for builders.

Perplexity Orchestrator


# Perplexity Launches Orchestrator API for Model Routing and Failover


By OpenTools Team


·


November 20, 2026


Perplexity opened its internal model‑routing layer to developers with the Orchestrator API, giving one endpoint for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI and open‑weight models with automatic same‑model failover and unified billing. Unlike OpenRouter's 5.5% fee, Perplexity charges no platform fee on credits.


## One Endpoint for Frontier and Open-Weight Models


Perplexity has opened the model-routing layer it already uses in production to outside developers. The **Orchestrator API** puts OpenAI,[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) , Google, xAI and open-weight models like GLM, Kimi and[DeepSeek](https://opentools.ai/organizations/deepseek) behind a single endpoint, according to[Perplexity](https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/blog/introducing-orchestrator) . It accepts OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages formats, so most teams only need to swap their API key and base URL, per[MarkTechPost](https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/11/19/perplexity-orchestrator-api-failover-model-routing/) .


Perplexity says it routes hundreds of millions of requests daily across more than 85 models and over a dozen providers. The company wrote that "through[one API](https://opentools.ai/tools/one-api) , teams can run simple, high-volume tasks on lower-cost models and reserve more powerful models for more demanding work."


## How Automatic Failover Works


Failover keeps the **model fixed** and swaps the deployment: a Claude request failing on[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) can be served by AWS Bedrock, for instance. It triggers on provider errors, rate limits and timeouts, and requests that fail before producing output are not billed, per[MarkTechPost](https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/11/19/perplexity-orchestrator-api-failover-model-routing/) .


[Perplexity](https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/blog/introducing-orchestrator) claims that in one month of production traffic, Claude and GPT requests through Orchestrator had higher success rates than any individual provider, with less daily variation during provider incidents. It's a meaningful claim: a success-rate bump from 99.0% to 99.99% can save thousands of failed responses for high-volume teams.


## Prompt-Based Routing in Preview


Orchestrator ships with a preview feature called **Routes** that lets developers describe in plain language which requests each model should handle. You set a default model, then define up to five routes with a name, description and model. A decision model reads the conversation and route descriptions — never the route names or model IDs — and picks where each request goes, per[MarkTechPost](https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/11/19/perplexity-orchestrator-api-failover-model-routing/) .


There's also an **Auto Effort** preview that dynamically adjusts how much reasoning a model uses on its next turn based on a developer-defined policy. An agent, for example, can spend more effort recovering from a tool error without switching models.


## Pricing: No Platform Fee, Tiered Access


Orchestrator bills at the answering model's published per-token rate regardless of which provider serves it, with **no additional platform fee** on credits, per[MarkTechPost](https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/11/19/perplexity-orchestrator-api-failover-model-routing/) . Access is tiered by cumulative credit purchases:


- **Tier 0** $0 — Google, xAI and open-weight models


- **Tier 1** $50 — OpenAI and most Anthropic models


- **Tier 2** $250 — Claude Opus 5, Opus 5.5 and Fable models

## What Builders Should Watch


The no-fee structure is the headline.[OpenRouter](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openrouter) charges a 5.5% standard fee on credit purchases, while Perplexity's Orchestrator passes through the model's list price with no markup — which could make it the cheaper default for teams already paying for Claude and GPT usage. The trade-off is control: Orchestrator does not support bring-your-own-key, and you cannot manually pick a deployment, per[MarkTechPost](https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/11/19/perplexity-orchestrator-api-failover-model-routing/) .


[Perplexity](https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/blog/introducing-orchestrator) positions Orchestrator as the first step in its API platform for intelligent model orchestration. For builders tired of managing multiple provider accounts, the pitch is simple: one key, one invoice, and the routing handled for you.
